# lnurlcash-kit

LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer note client for TypeScript. ESM-only, Node 22+,
browsers, Deno, Bun. MIT.

Install: npm install lnurlcash-kit

## What this is

LNURLcash notes are LUD-03 withdrawRequest links whose k1 IS the asset:
lnurlw://mint.example/w?k1=<32-byte-hex>&amount=<msat>. Whoever knows the k1
can spend it. Amounts are ALWAYS integer milli-satoshis.

Draft spec: https://github.com/lnurl/luds/pull/301
Reference mint: https://github.com/dni/lnurl-mint
Reference wallet: https://github.com/dni/lnurl-wallet

## Core API

resolveNoteInput(text) -> url | null    accepts bech32 LNURL, lnurlw://, https
fetchNoteInfo(url, opts?) -> {callback, k1, maxWithdrawable, mintPubkey}
rotateNote(callback, k1, opts?) -> {k1, signature}
splitNote(callback, k1s, amountMsat, opts?) -> {k1, change, signature, changeSignature}
mergeNotes(callback, k1s, opts?) -> {k1, signature}
meltNote(callback, k1, bolt11, opts?) -> {pr?, verify?}
settleNote(baseUrl, k1, expectedMsat, sig?, opts?) -> {k1, amountMsat, signature?, callback}
settleNoteForValue(noteUrl, {mints, minMsat, requireSignature?}, opts?)
  -> {note, newUrl}   server side: accept a note as payment, rotate to settle
probeBurnedNote(url, opts?) -> 'live' | 'gone' | 'unknown'
verifyNoteSignature(k1, amountMsat, sigHex, pubkeyHex | pubkeyHex[]) -> boolean
verifyNoteSignatureAgainst(k1, amountMsat, sigHex, keys) -> {valid, pubkey}
fetchMintAddress(url, opts?) -> {mintPubkey?, payLink, name?, motd?, contact?,
  tosUrl?, fees?, version?, previousPubkeys?, mintToHash?, node*?}
  experimental, often absent
  mintPubkey verifies note signatures. It is NOT the node key in nodeUri.
  nodePubkey is a deprecated alias for mintPubkey, dropped next breaking change.
  mintToHash is the fallback copy of the payRequest's flag - see 13.
deriveCashRoot(seedBytes) -> CashNode      LUD-25's scheme: BIP-32 m/139'
deriveCashDomainNode(root, host) -> CashNode   m/139'/d1/d2/d3/d4, d1..d4 =
  first 16 bytes of HMAC-SHA256(privkey at m/139'/0, host) as 4 raw uint32.
  RAW: BIP-32 reads >= 2^31 as hardened, so ~half the levels are, by the
  host name alone. Never mask the top bit, never harden all four - either
  derives a different tree and restores nothing, silently.
deriveCashSecret(root, host, index) -> k1  the hardened child i' of that node
cashSecretAt(domainNode, index) -> k1      no EC needed below the domain node,
  which is why a hardware signer is provisioned with the node, not the seed
cashSecretSource(root, host, start) -> RandomSecret & {index()}
cashNodeToHex/cashNodeFromHex             privateKey || chainCode, 64 bytes
deriveCashChild(node, rawUint32) -> CashNode   BIP-32 CKDpriv, for checking
  this library against BIP-32's own vectors
LUD-25 Part 2: a note keyed by a public key, spent by a recoverable signature
encodeCp1/decodeCp1/isCp1   note pubkey, 32-byte x-only, bech32m "cp"
encodeCk1/decodeCk1/isCk1   note bearer secret, 65-byte r||s||recid, "ck"
encodeCs1/decodeCs1/isCs1   mint certificate over hex(pk), same layout, "cs"
encodeCx1/decodeCx1/isCx1   watch-only branch {pubkeyXOnly, chainCode}, "cx"
  decoders return null, never throw; mixed case is refused (BIP-350)
deriveCashAddressNode(root, host) -> CashNode   m/139'/1'/d1..d4, hashing key
  m/139'/1'/0. The REFERENCE WALLET's path, not the spec text's m/139'/d1..d4
  (that is the Part 1 ladder's node, and finds none of its notes).
cashNodeToCx1(node) -> Cx1
deriveNotePubkey(P, chainCode, i) -> pk    watch-only, BIP-341 style tweak;
  i any uint32, 4-byte big-endian, never hardened
deriveNoteSecretKey(p, chainCode, i) -> sk negates p first when P has odd y
signNoteOwnership(sk) -> 65 bytes          RFC6979 over fixed "LNURLcash"
recoverNoteOwnershipPubkey(sig) -> pk | null
verifyNoteSignature also takes a ck1 as k1 and a cs1 as the signature
noteIdOf(k1) -> id | null   sha256(k1) for a secret, the recovered key for a
  ck1. One note has many valid ck1 strings: compare notes by this, not by k1
noteLookupOf(k1) -> string  hash, or cp1 for a ck1; for fetchNoteInfoByHash
Wire: a ck1 goes wherever a k1 does; a cp1 wherever an output does
  (requestInvoice h, *WithHash outputs: cp1 sent as p1/p2, hash as h/h2)
deriveNoteRoot(seedBytes) -> Uint8Array    LEGACY, pre-spec. Do not mint under
deriveNoteSecret(root, host, index) -> k1  it; still scanned so old notes live.
derivedSecretSource(root, host, start) -> RandomSecret & {index()}
restoreFromSeed(baseUrl, seed, host, {gap?, start?, probeK1?,
  allowSecretDisclosure?}, opts?) -> {found[] (.scheme), next: {bip32, hmac}}
  walks BOTH schemes. A by-hash walk CANNOT see a spent index (LUD-25 makes
  spent and never-issued the same answer), and a rotate burns the old index,
  so a wallet that rotated more than `gap` times scans as empty. The
  persisted per-host counter is the real backup; the scan is the fallback.
  The counter is not secret - back it up, and merge it upwards only.
restoreNotes(baseUrl, root, host, {gap?, start?}, opts?) -> {found[], next}
  legacy scheme only
fetchPayRequest(url, opts?) -> {callback, minSendable, maxSendable, metadata,
  withdrawLink?, mintFee?, mintToHash?}     mintToHash: mint accepts an `h`
fetchInvoiceVerification(url, opts?)
requestInvoice(cb, msat, {h?, ...opts}?) -> {pr, verify?, disposable, mintToHash}
claimMintedNote(withdrawLink, k1, opts?)
  -> {state: 'minted'|'unminted'|'pending'|'spent', k1, amountMsat, callback}
encodePaymentRequest(req) -> "lnurlcashreq1..."  base64url(JCS JSON), prefix
decodePaymentRequest(str, {now?}) -> PaymentRequest  throws ProtocolError
isPaymentRequest(str) -> boolean       true for an expired one too
paymentRequestAmountMsat(req) -> msat  request amount is in SAT, this is the
  only sat-denominated field in the library; never multiply by hand
parseMintFee(metadata) / applyMintFee(gross, fee) / grossUpForMintFee(net, fee)
createClient(opts) -> all of the above with opts bound

Options (always last): {fetch?, timeoutMs?, offline?, randomSecret?,
                        requireSignatures?, mutationRetries?}
  requireSignatures defaults true: refuse a mint that publishes no
  mintPubkey or returns an unsigned mutation. mutationRetries defaults 1:
  re-send a rotate/split/merge whose answer was lost, never a melt.

## Rules an implementation MUST follow

1. maxWithdrawable from fetchNoteInfo is the ONLY authoritative value. The
   `amount` in a note URL is an unverified claim.
2. On rotate/split/merge the WALLET generates the replacement secret and
   discloses only sha256(secret). Never accept a service-supplied k1.
3. On ANY error from a mutation call newSecretsOf(err) FIRST, persist what
   it returns, then call probeBurnedNote to learn what happened. Treating a
   failure as a failure destroys money the service may already have minted.
   AmbiguousMutationError always carries secrets; so does UnverifiableNoteError,
   and so does a NoteSpentError or NoteUnknownError from a mutation, because
   that is also what a retried GET looks like at a service that has not
   implemented the replay rule.
4. RequestRefusedError means nothing was sent - safe to treat as no-op.
5. A melt's OK means IN FLIGHT, not spent. PendingNoteError means retry, not
   spent.
5b. Offline verification is MANDATORY. A conforming service publishes
   mintPubkey on every withdrawRequest and returns sig (and sig2 on a split)
   from every rotate/split/merge. This library refuses a service that does
   not; UnverifiableNoteError means the mutation LANDED unsigned, so keep its
   secrets. Opt out per call with requireSignatures: false.
5c. A retried rotate/split/merge MUST be answered by the service as a replay
   of the original success, so re-sending one whose answer was lost is safe
   and usually completes it. Re-send the IDENTICAL request: the replay is
   matched on the k1 set, h, h2 and amount, so a fresh secret makes it a
   different mutation and a second real burn. Never re-send a melt.
6. Rotate immediately after claiming a minted note: the mint generated that
   preimage, and LUD-21 verify exposes it to anyone who saw the invoice.
   Does not apply to a note minted with `h` - see 13.
7. Never log note URLs. The secret is in the query string.
8. Never branch on error message text. Branch on the error class.
9. lnurlcashreq1 means ONE schema: {v: 1, id (16 hex), amount (whole sat as
   a decimal string), currency: "sat", methodDetails: {mints}, to?, memo?,
   expires?}, JCS-canonicalised, base64url, no padding. Validation is
   strict, an unrecognised field included. At the expiry is expired. Pass
   {now: 0} to show a user what they scanned. The decoder also reads the
   short {a, m, u} form an early 402 rail emitted under this prefix, but
   NEVER emit it.
10. Accepting a note as payment MUST end in a rotate. Checking its value
    and granting access without rotating leaves the payer able to spend it
    again; the rotate is both the ownership transfer and the replay check.
11. A mint may rotate its signing key. Verify against its current key plus
    the previousPubkeys it publishes; a note that verifies only against a
    retired key should be rotated to be re-signed. An empty key list is a
    rejection.
12. With derived secrets, persist the per-host counter in the SAME write
    that stages the new records and BEFORE the hash goes on the wire. A
    split consumes two indices, a rotate one; read source.index() for the
    next unused one. Bumping late re-derives a secret the mint has already
    seen.
13. Name the note you are buying where the mint offers it. Read mintToHash
    off fetchPayRequest FIRST (fetchMintAddress is the fallback for a mint
    that only says it on that optional document), then derive a secret,
    persist it, and pass h = hashK1(secret) to requestInvoice. The mint
    credits the note at that hash, the payment preimage is then not a valid
    k1, and you claim with claimMintedNote rather than polling verify - no
    rotate needed, and the note is seed-derived from birth so restoreNotes
    finds it. Persist the secret BEFORE requesting the invoice. Three
    places carry the flag: the payRequest and the mint address both mean
    "I accept an h", InvoiceResult.mintToHash means "I bound THIS quote to
    your hash". Anything not exactly true is no. A mint that advertises
    nowhere ignores the h and the preimage path is unchanged.

## Error classes

RequestRefusedError    nothing sent, note untouched
ServiceRejectedError   processed and refused (definitive)
  PendingNoteError     a melt is in flight on this k1 - retry
  NoteSpentError       authoritative: already burned - but from a MUTATION at
                       a service that will not replay a retry, it may be a
                       retry whose first attempt landed; read
                       newSecretsOf(err) before believing it
  NoteUnknownError     service does not recognise it
AmbiguousMintError     outcome UNKNOWN - assume nothing
  AmbiguousMutationError  carries .newSecrets - persist them
UnverifiableNoteError  the mutation LANDED and came back unsigned. The note is
                       real; carries .newSecrets - persist them
newSecretsOf(err) -> string[]  the secrets any error is carrying, or none
ProtocolError          a non-mutating response did not match the spec, which
                       includes a withdrawRequest publishing no mintPubkey

## Conformance

Vectors and an adversarial mock mint:
https://github.com/lnurlcash/lnurlcash-conformance
